subject: y axis numbers on right hand side

messages.author: bf88c5bfbffaf252
messages.subject: y axis numbers on right hand side
parts:
Hi,

I would like to replicate a bloomberg tick data graph (as attached):

1) I would like to be able to put the numbers that are on the y-axis on the right hand side, rather than the left,
2) I would ideally like pointers representing the last points of each path
3) I would like to ensure that the times match up/line up vertically without having to use facets (as the numbers on the y-axis at the moment are causing it not to line up)
4) I would also like to get a gradient fill for the background to match bloomberg

I have got quite close in replicating,but I am missing the above. Please see attached R plot.

regards

HLM

messages.subject: Re: y axis numbers on right hand side
parts:
Hi,

This might help,

http://stackoverflow.com/questions/17492230/how-to-place-grobs-with-annotation-custom-at-precise-areas-of-the-plot-region/17493256#17493256

as for the gradient, easiest way might be to add a background image,

gradient <- matrix(grey(seq(0.5, 1, length=100)), ncol=1)

qplot(1:10, rnorm(10), geom="blank") +
  annotation_raster(gradient, interpolate=TRUE,
                    xmin=-Inf, xmax=Inf, ymin=-Inf, ymax=Inf) +
  geom_point()

HTH,

b.

On 12 July 2013 07:43, hlm <hideyos...@gmail.com> wrote:
Thanks for that!

Is there a way to get the grid lines both major and minor back when using annotation_raster?

The sane answer would be no, I guess. 

Consider this, however,

background = function(gradient=matrix(grey(seq(0.5, 1, length=100)), ncol=1)) {
  structure(
    list(gradient=gradient),
    class = c("element_background","element_blank", "element") 
  )
}

element_grob.element_background <- function(element, ...)  {
 rasterGrob(element$gradient, width=unit(1,"npc"), height=unit(1,"npc"))

geom_point() +
  theme(panel.background=background())


It's an ugly hack though, not to be recommended. See https://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/issues/808 for further details.

HTH,

b.
